debt.sit_ground: $6,400 on one card at 24% APR. Paying the $140 minimum, about $110 of it goes to interest. Been stuck at this balance for a year.
debt.sit_against:
Eating out when tired (about $280 a month)
No budget, I check the balance and hope
Autopay only covers the minimum
debt.sit_for:
Steady paycheck every two weeks
Spouse is on board
I finished boot camp, I can do hard things for 12 months
debt.sit_terrain: Free time is 8–9 PM after the kid is down. Holidays in December will be the hardest stretch.
debt.mis_what: pay off the $6,400 on my Visa
debt.mis_why: stop losing $110 a month to interest and sleep at night
debt.exe_intent: Card at $0, still open but not carried. A one-page budget we both look at weekly, and $1,000 in savings so a flat tire doesn't go back on the card.
debt.exe_p1: Weeks 1–2: list every bill, cancel 2 subscriptions, build $500 starter savings
debt.exe_p2: Months 1–10: $600 a month to the card, autopay set on payday
debt.exe_p3: Months 11–12: finish the card, grow savings to $1,000
debt.exe_daily:
Log every purchase in the notes app (30 seconds)
Pack lunch Mon–Thu
Sunday: 10-minute money check with my spouse
debt.exe_ifthen:
If I eat out, then it comes out of next week's fun money, not the card
If a surprise bill hits, then savings covers it and I pause extra payments one month
If I miss a Sunday check, then we do it Monday night, no skipping two
debt.sus_fuel: In bed by 10:30. Tired me spends money.
debt.sus_supply: Free budget sheet. Cut streaming ($32) and the gym I don't use ($45).
debt.sus_support: Spouse. A free credit counseling call if I get stuck.
debt.cmd_partner: Marcus, text every Sunday with the balance
debt.cmd_checkin: Daily: log purchases. Weekly: Sunday money check. Monthly: screenshot the balance.
debt.cmd_signals:
I stop logging purchases
I avoid opening the card app
Two takeout nights in a row
debt.cmd_password: So my family never pays a bank for my bad week.

fit.sit_ground: 40 lb over where I felt good. Winded on stairs. Haven't run since I got out three years ago.
fit.sit_against:
Late-night snacking
Knee aches on long runs
No set workout time
fit.sit_for:
I know how to train
A park two streets over
A friend who also wants to get moving
fit.sit_terrain: Mornings before work, 5:45–6:30. Weekends are open until 9.
fit.mis_what: lose 20 lb and run a 5K without stopping
fit.mis_where: at the park and at home
fit.mis_why: keep up with my son and feel like myself again
fit.exe_intent: Moving 4 days a week out of habit, not willpower. Eating mostly at home. A finished 5K with a time on paper.
fit.exe_p1: Weeks 1–3: walk 30 minutes, 4 mornings a week. Stop eating after 8 PM.
fit.exe_p2: Weeks 4–10: run/walk intervals, bodyweight circuit twice a week
fit.exe_p3: Weeks 11–16: run 3 miles straight, sign up for a local 5K
fit.exe_daily:
Shoes by the door the night before
Water bottle filled before bed
Protein at breakfast
fit.exe_ifthen:
If my knee hurts, then I bike or swim that day
If I sleep through the alarm, then 15 minutes at lunch
If I blow a meal, then the next one is normal, no 'starting Monday'
fit.sus_fuel: Lights out by 10. Meal prep Sunday for 4 lunches.
fit.sus_supply: Running shoes ($90). Free run/walk app. Nothing else needed.
fit.sus_support: Doctor checkup before week 4. Run buddy on Saturdays.
fit.cmd_partner: Dee, Saturday runs and a weekly weigh-in text
fit.cmd_checkin: Daily: check the box on the calendar. Weekly: Saturday run and weigh-in.
fit.cmd_signals:
Two missed mornings in a row
Shoes not by the door
Snacking after 9

career.sit_ground: EAS in 6 months. Resume is my military record. No civilian job offers yet.
career.sit_against:
Military jargon on my resume
No network outside the service
I don't know what I want to do
career.sit_for:
GI Bill and SkillBridge eligibility
Leadership and logistics experience
Security clearance (current)
career.sit_terrain: Evenings and one weekend day. Two field ops coming up in month 2.
career.mis_what: land a full-time civilian job offer
career.mis_why: start civilian life with a paycheck and no gap
career.exe_intent: A signed offer before my last day, in a field I picked on purpose, with a plan for school if I want it.
career.exe_p1: Month 1: pick 2 target jobs, translate resume, set up LinkedIn
career.exe_p2: Months 2–4: 3 coffee chats a week, apply to SkillBridge, 5 applications a week
career.exe_daily:
One message to a veteran working in my target field
One application or follow-up
Friday: update my tracker
career.exe_ifthen:
If I'm in the field, then I queue messages before I go
If I get rejected, then I ask for feedback and send two more
If nothing moves in 6 weeks, then I change the target, not the effort
career.sus_fuel: Keep PT up. It's the best stress relief I have.
career.sus_supply: Free resume help at the base transition office. One interview outfit.
career.sus_support: Transition counselor. Two Marines who got out last year.
career.cmd_partner: Sgt. Ruiz (ret.), call every other Sunday
career.cmd_checkin: Weekly: Friday tracker review. Every other Sunday: call with my mentor.
career.cmd_signals:
No messages sent in 3 days
Avoiding the tracker
Saying 'I'll figure it out after I get out'

parent.sit_ground: I'm home every night but on my phone most of it. My 2-year-old asks me to play and I say 'in a minute'.
parent.sit_against:
Phone in my hand after work
Work stress follows me home
Tired by 7 PM
parent.sit_for:
Bedtime is a routine I already do
My spouse wants this too
Weekends are mostly free
parent.sit_terrain: 5:30–7:30 PM weekdays is family time. Saturdays mornings are ours.
parent.mis_what: give my son 30 phone-free minutes every day
parent.mis_why: be the dad he remembers playing with
parent.exe_intent: He runs to me when I get home. My phone lives in a drawer at dinner. My spouse gets a break every evening.
parent.exe_p1: Weeks 1–2: phone in the drawer 5:30–6:30, sit on the floor and follow his lead
parent.exe_p2: Weeks 3–8: one outside adventure every Saturday morning
parent.exe_p3: Weeks 9–12: I own bath and bedtime 4 nights a week
parent.exe_daily:
Phone in drawer at the front door
One book at bedtime, his pick
Ask my spouse: what can I take off your plate?
parent.exe_ifthen:
If work calls, then I step out, handle it, and come back. No 'quick scroll'
If I'm wiped out, then quiet play on the floor still counts
parent.sus_fuel: Eat a snack before I walk in the door. Hungry dad is short-tempered dad.
parent.sus_supply: A drawer. A park pass. Library card for books.
parent.sus_support: My spouse. A dads' group at church. A counselor if the stress stays heavy.
parent.cmd_partner: My spouse, quick check after bedtime
parent.cmd_checkin: Daily: 30 minutes done? Weekly: Sunday night, what worked.
parent.cmd_signals:
He stops asking me to play
Phone at the dinner table
Snapping over small things
